query: Which studies by Sergio García-Carrión and collaborators recover experimental designs from historical industrial data? Start from 'Retrospective DoE Methodology for Guiding Process Optimization from Historical Data' (ENBIS 2023) and Ferrer, Borràs-Ferrís and García-Carrión (2025), DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-96736-8_6. Identify related journal articles or later developments, distinguishing them from conference abstracts.
follow_ups: Which publications describe how this research selects observations near factorial design points, chooses matching tolerances, handles missing treatment combinations, and checks consistency across reconstructed designs? Look for full methodological accounts beyond conference abstracts.

Which studies validate or critique retrospective factorial fitting and its use for planning subsequent experiments? Focus on aliasing, rank deficiency, uncertainty from imputed cells, and what additional assumptions are required for causal interpretation.

query: Which studies use association rules, frequent itemsets or rule induction to select experimental designs from existing databases? Start from Parpoula et al. (2014), 'Supersaturated plans for variable selection in large databases', DOI 10.19139/soic.v2i2.75. Find extensions and separate historical subset selection from selection of genuinely new experimental runs.
follow_ups: Which follow-up studies extend rule-based retrospective design selection beyond main-effect screening to interactions, continuous factors, functional data or constrained design spaces?

Which papers compare association-rule-guided design selection with optimal subsampling or design selection using the same data without rules? Look for matched sample budgets and separate statistical benefits from computational savings.

query: Which methods use factor-to-factor association rules, subgroup discovery or contrast-set mining to identify local dependencies, poorly covered factor combinations or missing experimental contrasts in historical process data? Focus on diagnosing the observed operating policy rather than predicting product quality.
follow_ups: Which methods distinguish physically forbidden factor combinations from combinations missing because of operator habits, machine assignment or historical operating policies? Look for process constraints and expert validation of inferred rules.

Which studies show that local or conditional rule-based diagnostics find missing contrasts missed by global correlations, matrix-rank checks or standard overlap diagnostics? Identify the conditions under which rules add useful information.

query: Which causal rule mining methods distinguish compound-exposure associations from causal interactions and heterogeneous treatment effects? Start from Li et al., 'From Observational Studies to Causal Rule Mining', DOI 10.1145/2746410, and include subsequent work on causal interactions and subgroup treatment effects.
follow_ups: Which identification assumptions do these methods require concerning confounding, positivity, treatment assignment and variable timing? Find analyses of failure under unmeasured confounding or adjustment for post-treatment variables.

Which methods test interaction contrasts rather than only the association of a conjunction with an outcome? Examine whether rule-pruning strategies can remove genuine effect heterogeneity or interactions.

query: Which studies combine functional PCA of batch-process response curves with retrospective or prospective experimental design? Include Fidaleo (2020), DOI 10.1007/s11947-020-02449-2. Focus on functional responses, response-surface models for component scores, and reconstruction of trajectories under different experimental conditions.
follow_ups: Which studies compare multivariate functional PCA with unfolded PCA for industrial batch monitoring, including Sergio García-Carrión and collaborators' work on monitoring and fault diagnosis of batch processes? Look for evidence about information retained by each representation.

Which papers use functional response representations to choose additional experimental runs or improve estimation of treatment contrasts? Distinguish that objective from monitoring, fault detection and prediction on previously observed operating conditions.

query: Which optimal experimental design methods choose physically feasible functional inputs, such as feeding or temperature profiles, for scalar or functional responses? Include Michaelides et al. (2026), DOI 10.1093/biomtc/ujaf169, and May et al. (2026), DOI 10.1007/s11749-026-01004-z.
follow_ups: Which methods impose constraints on profile levels, rates of change, total dose, monotonicity or the number of switches? Find studies comparing functional principal components with physically constrained basis expansions for generating candidate experiments.

Which experimental-design studies distinguish assigned control profiles from measured process trajectories affected by feedback or intermediate outcomes? Focus on when a proposed intervention on functional scores corresponds to an executable process intervention.

query: When can FPCA of historical process trajectories miss information relevant to new experiments because influential directions have low variance or were never independently excited? Find studies comparing unsupervised FPCA with supervised functional dimension reduction, functional PLS or penalized functional regression.
follow_ups: Which theoretical or empirical studies address predictive information in low-variance functional components? Include Cai and Yuan (2012), DOI 10.1080/01621459.2012.716337, and distinguish weakly observed directions from directions entirely absent from the historical data.

Which studies distinguish treatment-induced timing changes from nuisance phase variation in functional data? Identify when curve registration removes the effect of interest and how amplitude and phase can be modeled separately.

query: Which experimental-design methods use historical observational process data to choose new interventions that distinguish confounded factors or competing response models? Include methods that account for observational bias and changes between historical and new data, such as Gao et al.'s R-Design (2026), DOI 10.1145/3770855.3817762.
follow_ups: Which methods use bridge runs, repeated reference conditions or contemporary controls to separate factor interactions from differences between historical and newly collected data? Look for temporal drift, batch effects and changing operating policies.

Which studies compare observationally informed design with D-, I- or c-optimal augmentation and model-discrimination design under matched experimental budgets? Focus on uncertainty in scientific contrasts and robustness to model misspecification.

query: Which methods provide valid statistical error control for association-rule or pattern discovery in clustered, longitudinal or industrial batch data? Focus on multiple testing, discovery versus confirmation samples, adaptive discretization and dependence between measurements from the same experimental unit.
follow_ups: Which studies evaluate rule discovery when preprocessing, functional dimension reduction and threshold selection are learned from the data? Look for validation that separates entire batches or production campaigns rather than individual time points.

Which methods assess rule stability under changes in discretization, latent-variable basis or FPCA orientation? Find approaches that compare selected observations or reconstructed curve regions rather than only the exact text of a rule.

query: Which published methods are closest to using interpretable association rules learned from historical functional process data to choose feasible new experiments that resolve confounding or distinguish competing response models? Include retrospective DoE, subgroup discovery, active learning and optimal design, even when authors use different terminology.
follow_ups: Which papers directly compare rule-guided experimental selection with the same representation and selection objective without rules? Look for ablation studies that separate representation quality, statistical information, interpretability and computational cost.

Which publicly available datasets or process simulators contain trajectories together with independently varied or randomized controls? Find benchmarks suitable for evaluating retrospective design against known effects or held-out interventions, rather than prediction on observational data alone.
